title: Accept a roadmap preamble in an import outline
lead:
Prose between a `# Roadmap` title and the first `##` item is refused with
"text before the first '##' item; a document title needs a single '#'"
(`src/slicer/outline.py`, ~lines 170-173). The title was present. The
message tells the writer to add the line they already wrote, and says
nothing about where roadmap-wide context actually goes. `apply_outline`
can store a preamble (`src/slicer/ops.py`, ~lines 818-819) but `cmd_import`
never passes one. `slicer prose edit preamble` is the only supported way
to set it.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** goals, non-goals, epilogue, or per-pass prose in the outline. The `#` title line stays ignored.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
An outline is supposed to be the whole roadmap in one file. Context under
the title is the preamble readers see above the queue. Rejecting it with a
hint about the title sends people looking for a format problem they do not
have. Accepting that prose makes the import match the file they tried to
write. Rewording the error alone would still drop the paragraph on the
floor.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/outline.py` — `parse` (~lines 106-174); it currently returns only the item list
- `src/slicer/cli.py` — `cmd_import` (~line 198)
- `src/slicer/ops.py` — `apply_outline`'s existing `preamble` argument, and `_slice_from_source` for `promote`
- `docs/import.md` — the shape section, next to the rule that a `#` title is ignored
- `tests/test_outline.py`, `tests/test_import.py`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. An outline whose body is a `#` title, a paragraph, then `##` items imports. The paragraph becomes `index.preamble`. The title line is not part of it. Items import as they do today.
2. `--dry-run` reports that preamble and writes nothing.
3. A second import whose preamble differs from a non-empty preamble already stored is refused, nothing written, until `--force`.
4. An outline with no leading prose leaves the existing preamble alone.
5. `promote --file` rejects leading prose and names `slicer prose edit preamble`. Promoting one slice must not rewrite roadmap prose.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Keep the single `#` title ignored. Treat the other text before the first `##` item as the roadmap preamble: return it from `parse` beside the specs (both callers today are `cmd_import` and `promote`'s `_slice_from_source`). `import` passes it to `apply_outline`. On apply, set `index.preamble` when the outline has that prose. If the stored preamble is already non-empty and different, add a problem and write nothing unless `--force`, same as a duplicate title. No leading prose means do not touch the preamble.

`promote --file` does not take a preamble. If the source has leading prose, refuse it with an error that points at `slicer prose edit preamble`.

Document the shape in `docs/import.md`: context under the title is the preamble, and goals, non-goals, and the epilogue stay on `slicer prose`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: A file that starts with `# Roadmap`, a short intro, and then items imports the intro as the preamble and the items as the queue. `slicer check` passes.
